Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public. 




Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan 
"The Right to Information, The Right to Live"

IS:9699-1981 




Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
CHISEL, DENTAL, LARGE 



( Reaffirmed 1998) 



1. Scope — Prescribes dimensional and other requirements for large size chisels used in dentistry. 

2. Shape and Dimensions — As shown in Fig. 1.

All dimensions in millimetres. 
FIG. 1 CHISEL, DENTAL, LARGE 

2-1 The tolerances on various dimensions shall be ± 0'2 mm for dimensions up to 10 mm; and 
± 1 mm for dimensions above 10 mm. 

3. Material — Stainless steel conforming to designation 40CM3 of IS : 6603-1972 'Specification for 
stainless steel bars and flats '. 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The cutting edge of the instrument shall be properly sharpened. 

4.2 The chisel shall be free from burrs, feathers, nicks, waviness and other tool mark. 

4.3 The chisel shall be polished bright and passivated. 

4.4 All the edges shall be suitably rounded except the cutting edge. 

5. Heat Treatment — The chisel shall be hardened and tempered to a hardness of 520 to 620 HV. 

6. Tests 

6.1 Performance — The chisel shall be tested by chiselling a fresh long sheep bone with a moderate 
pressure. The chisel shall do this easily and cleanly. This shall be repeated five times. The 
edges of working end of chisel shall not show any sign of damage after the test. 

6.2 Corrosion Resistance — The chisel shall be tested for corrosion resistance as mentioned 
in IS : 7531-1975 'Method for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless 
steel surgical instruments \ The chisel shall not show any sign of corrosion.

IS : 9699 - 1981 

7. Marking — The chisel shall be marked with manufacturer's name, initials or registered trade* 
mark, and size. 

7.1 ISI Certification Marking — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — The cutting edge shall be preserved by dipping In 'plastipeel'. The Instruments 
shall be put in a polyethylene bag or wrapped in wax paper and packed in carton. The Instrument 
may aiso be packed as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 



Printed at Arcee Preee, New Delhi, India
